messages:
Alex Chen: heads up — we're seeing pager errors after the 3.1 SDK rollout to canary. paging clients start failing with cursor/deserialization errors around the second page.
Jordan (oncall): on it. can you paste an example error?
Alex Chen: log snippet: `ERROR paginate: cursor deserialize failed: version mismatch: expected v2 got v3 (payload len 72)` — stacktrace attached in logs.
Samir: this is consistent with the change that switched cursor serialization to include an encoded timestamp. iirc we gated that behind a flag but apparently the flag wasn't set in canary agent images.
Emily - Support: I'm seeing customer reports from two teams — search-prod and insights-runner — both report repeated 400s when requesting page 2+. support ticket IDs: SUP-8012, SUP-8013. customers say clients get stuck and retry spams.
Raj Patel: timeline? when was the canary rolled?
Alex Chen: canary deploy started 09:12 UTC (~thread_ts). errors spiked at 09:17.
Jordan (oncall): incident-bot, create incident for paging regression from SDK 3.1 canary.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-03-15-042 — Paging cursor serialization regression affecting canary. Severity: P2.
Maya OpsBot: auto-alert: 4 errors/min from canary pool, 95th latency increased 120ms.
Jordan (oncall): quick mitigation: toggle kill-flag for the new cursor format so old clients don't get the new serialization. Alex, do we have a feature flag?
Alex Chen: yes, `feature.serialized_cursor_v3` — default true in the new build. We should set it false for canary and block rollout.
Samir: command to flip flag in prod config service: ```bash
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://config.prod.internal/flags/feature.serialized_cursor_v3 -d '{"value": false}'
```
Jordan (oncall): doing it now.
Alex Chen: also preparing rollback of the canary image to 3.0 for the canary pool if flag flip doesn't cut it.
deploy-bot: feature.serialized_cursor_v3 set to false by jordan (oncall) at 09:24 UTC.
Maya OpsBot: flag change acknowledged. error rate dropping but some retries ongoing.
Emily - Support: messaging to impacted customers: "We're rolling back a canary change affecting pagination and implementing a hotfix. Expect request success within 10-15 minutes; we're monitoring and will follow up." Sent to SUP-8012 and SUP-8013 at 09:26.
Jordan (oncall): we need to confirm no data loss and that cursor migrations are backward compatible. Samir, confirm schema difference is only extra timestamp appended, so older clients should ignore it if they don't parse?
Samir: unfortunately older client expects exact payload length; they fail on unknown fields. that's the root cause. We'll need a protocol-stable approach for future but short-term: rollback or force old serialization.
Raj Patel: escalate to release lead — we can't let this reach more clusters. Raj -> @deploy-lead.
Alex Chen: attempting canary rollback now: `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/canary inference-container=redwood/inference:3.0.7`
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for canary pool by alex. Estimated 3-5 minutes.
Maya OpsBot: canary rollback completed at 09:35 UTC. error rate back to baseline. 95th latency normalized.
Jordan (oncall): Good. We will block 3.1 rollout until a fix + compatibility test. Action items: 1) revert default flag in release branch, 2) add a compatibility unit test for cursor deserialization, 3) hotfix patch that supports both v2 and v3 cursors.
Samir: working on a tolerant parser now — it will try v3 then fallback to v2 parsing. patch ready in branch `fix/cursor-tolerant-parse`.
Alex Chen: QA, can you validate tolerant parser against recorded customer cursors (from SUP tickets) before we re-release?
Emily - Support: collecting sample cursors from customers and anonymizing; will hand to QA in ~30m.
Jordan (oncall): on-call handoff in 30 minutes to @oncall-next. I'll summarize: paging regression in 3.1 canary due to cursor serialization change leaked into canary images. Kill-flag used to mitigate; canary rolled back. Support notified. Follow-ups: compatibility parser + stricter gating for serialized format changes.
Raj Patel: also prep postmortem template: include timeline, customer impact, decision to rollback, and checklist for release flags. I'll open the doc once the group agrees.
Samir: quick patch PR posted -> https://git.internal/redwood/inference/pull/4567 — includes tolerant parser + unit tests.
Alex Chen: once PR merges, we should run a limited canary with the tolerant build + feature flag off, then enable flag only after compatibility tests pass.
deploy-bot: PR merged by samir at 10:12 UTC. CI green.
Maya OpsBot: staging canary deploy scheduled at 10:25 UTC.
Emily - Support: customer follow-up sent: "We're deploying a fix and will verify your jobs. We'll update you within the hour."
Jordan (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall: monitor SUP ticket queue, watch canary error rate, and be ready to flip `feature.serialized_cursor_v3` back to false if anything spikes.
Alex Chen: tagging for post-incident review: @pm_raj @sre_jordan @samir @emily-support.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: resolved -> rollback + compatibility patch. Root cause: serialization format change not gated in runtime canary config.
Raj Patel: opening postmortem doc now: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-03-15-042-postmortem (draft).
Emily - Support: closing SUP-8012 and SUP-8013 as customers acknowledged workaround.
Jordan (oncall): thanks everyone. We'll run the retrospective tomorrow AM.
Alex Chen: small note for release process — add an integration test that runs mixed-client deserialization across top-3 customer cursor formats.
Samir: agreed. will add to release checklist.
Jordan (oncall): handing off to oncall-next with thread pinned. good job triage team. :thumbsup:
